name: Azure damselfly
note: Azure damselflies (docs 12, 13 'The year, season by season'; M2 season marker, approved by Matt on 2026-10-20): slim sky-blue and black damselflies that flutter low among the reeds of any still pond and perch on the stems more than they fly. Several at a time, never named. A season marker: no gift, and they never count toward a tier milestone. LIFE. ecology: kind swarm (src/world/creatures/swarms.js, the dragonflies' model); dormancy names the window in recipes/world/seasons.json (the first ones climb out at the very end of spring, and they fly through the summer; the rest of the year they are nymphs in the pond). needs (src/world/ecology/needs.js): water: still fresh water depthM deep in a body of at least body.minM2 (fish are fine, so there is no pond rule, unlike the dragonflies'), full within okM, none beyond maxM. food: the midge field over a square of radiusM, against per times the ideal group. shelter: reeds above all, then rushes and iris, the best within radiusM, from 'from' and full at 'full'; weighted most, since a pond with no stems has nothing for them to perch on or lay their eggs in. quiet: low. company: n[0] to n[2], n[1] ideal. scored: any open ground or fresh water (where: near), for the margin and its stems. arrival (as the dragonflies'): a pond is right once its best square scores rightScore and it has room for startCount, for rightHoldH hours; after scoutAfterH, on a late morning (comeAtH) while they fly, a few may come (scoutChance a day, surely by maxWaitDays); one per m2PerOne square meters of good water, up to company n[2]; they settle after settleAfterH at settleMood and grow by growShare of the room left each day in the seasons growSeasons allows. In their dormancy window nothing changes, and they come back each year.
_look: LOOK. body: a blended-SDF azure damselfly in real meters (about 33 mm nose to tail), body-local +z forward, origin at the middle of the thorax: a wide head with an eye at each side (a damselfly's eyes are set far apart, never touching), a small thorax, and a long thin abdomen in ten segments, sky blue (blue) with a black band (black) at the end of segments two to seven and a black tip; four narrow stalked wings, each on its own bone (wing.fl, wing.fr, wing.hl, wing.hr). The abdomen is a little thicker than life (1.4 mm, not 1 mm) and the wings about 0.6 mm, so the mesh keeps them at its coarser levels of detail. displayScale 3 (Matt, 2026-10-21: drawn larger so players can find them; a little more than the dragonflies, being smaller); contactShadow 0. albedo (physical, linear; the palette is applied at the tonemap): the azure's pale sky blue, black bands, dark blue-green eyes, clear wings. motion (src/world/creatures/patrol.js; live only): kind patrol, as the dragonflies' but weak and low: a small beat (beatM) close over the margin, hovering only a moment (hoverS) hoverHeightM over the water or ground, short slow flits at up to dartMps; most of the time it rests on a reed, rush or iris stem within perchReachM (perchChance after each hover, perchS seconds), low on the stem (perchShare of its height); at rest the wings fold back together along the abdomen (each turned on edge by restRoll, raised restLift, then swept back restFold radians), never held open as a dragonfly's are. wings beat wingHz (hovering, flitting), swinging wingSwing radians, fore and hind pairs nearly together (hindLag). A startle sends it up to fleeHeightM for fleeS seconds. They are not curious (no visits). presence (doc 23): ringM, calmSpeed, editReachM. find: tap within tapM (plus tapPerM per meter away), or keep one within lookM of the middle of the view, zoomed in to lookDistM, for holdS seconds.
